method: 1527 Schleitheim primary print/text plus Sattler correspondence plus source-critical mapping of early trial accounts; later martyrology explicitly segregated

important_deltas.finding: The 1527 Schleitheim print/text is placed ahead of later confessional and martyrdom retellings.
Sattler's letter to Bucer and Capito supplies participant evidence for the theological dispute before the martyrdom narrative.
Sattler's authorship is retained as a leading-role attribution while the confession's own voice remains collective.
Graphic execution details from Martyrs Mirror are not promoted to contemporary evidence without an independent early locator.
Admiration for Sattler's courage remains separate from editorial evaluation of Schleitheim pacifism and civil-authority conclusions.

unsupported_popular_claims.claim: Every graphic detail in the later Martyrs Mirror account is a contemporary eyewitness transcript of Sattler's execution.
Sattler alone authored Schleitheim as a purely personal manifesto.
Martyrdom itself proves every Schleitheim doctrine biblically correct.

claim_upgrade_conditions.claim: specific graphic execution detail as exact contemporary fact
claim_upgrade_conditions.upgrade_requires: independent 1527 or closely contemporary trial/execution source with exact matching detail and locator
contemporary documentary evidence identifying Sattler as sole author rather than leading compiler/participant

visual_plan.concept: Sattler letter to Bucer and Capito as pre-martyrdom participant document
